title: Salmon with Beurre Blanc
subtitle: Pan-seared salmon with a classic French butter sauce
excerpt: Beurre blanc is a classic French butter sauce built on a sharp reduction of vinegar and onion into which cold butter is whisked piece by piece. It looks impressive but takes only 10 minutes. Here it is served alongside pan-seared salmon.
sourceNotes: Beurre blanc originated in the Loire Valley in France in the early twentieth century. It is attributed to a cook named Clemence Lefeuvre who reportedly made it by accident when forgetting to add eggs to a bearnaise.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The reduction can be made an hour ahead. Whisk in the butter just before serving.

content.text: The butter must be very cold when it goes into the sauce. Cut it into small cubes and keep it in the fridge until the moment you need it. Whisk over the lowest possible heat and never let the sauce boil or it will split.
Make the reduction first. Put the diced onion and white wine vinegar in a small saucepan. Bring to the boil and simmer until the liquid has reduced to about 1 tablespoon. Remove from the heat.

Season the salmon on both sides. Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Place the salmon skin-side down and press gently with a fish slice for the first 30 seconds. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the skin is crisp and golden.
Flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more for medium. Transfer to warm plates.
Return the reduction to the lowest possible heat. Whisk in the cold butter cubes one at a time, adding each piece just as the previous one has melted. Do not let the sauce boil.
Add the lemon juice and chives, taste for seasoning, and spoon over the salmon at once.

items.cause: Heat too high or butter added too fast.
items.fix: Whisk in an ice cube or a splash of cold water off the heat.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough or skin was wet.
items.fix: Pat dry and press the skin flat in a hotter pan.
